Thought: I need to determine the most common physical form of carbamates. Carbamates are a class of organic compounds derived from carbamic acid (NH2COOH). Let me think about their general properties.

Carbamates typically have the structure R-O-CO-NR2, where R represents various organic groups. Most carbamates are crystalline solids at room temperature due to their molecular structure and intermolecular forces. While some specific carbamates might be liquids depending on their specific structure, the majority are solids. They are generally not gases or highly volatile compounds.

Based on my knowledge of organic chemistry, carbamates are predominantly found as solids at standard conditions.
Final Answer: Carbamates are a class of organic compounds derived from carbamic acid. Most carbamates have relatively high molecular weights and strong intermolecular forces (including hydrogen bonding in many cases), which results in them typically being crystalline solids at room temperature. While some specific carbamates with lower molecular weights might be liquids, the vast majority are solids.
